data.narrative:
TerraPower is a late-stage nuclear energy company founded by Bill Gates that has raised $1.7B+ to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises 10 identified peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private companies including Helion, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy—though no sufficiently deep same-stage cohort exists for direct median benchmarking.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $1.7B total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage progression, this method yields $2.0B. The Peer-Median approach does not apply: while 6 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier companies yields insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3) to generate a meaningful median. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material noise given the specialized nature of advanced nuclear technology.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B (low) to $2.3B (median to high), centered on $2.0B. This range reflects stage-appropriate valuation progression but carries meaningful uncertainty around deployment risk, regulatory pathway clarity, and the absence of comparable late-stage nuclear technology valuations. The single-method result should be weighted accordingly; external validation through management guidance or recent financing terms would materially improve conviction in this range.
